tagline.text: Cebu's coffee capital, a mountain municipality of river gorges and springs in the west

location.label: Location
location.text: Tuburan, northwestern Cebu Island (about 82 km from Cebu City)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500–3,500 (per person, one night, lodging and transport included)

children.text: Tuburan is a mountain municipality in western Cebu called the "Coffee Capital of Cebu," with more than 3,000 hectares of coffee farms. A coffee farm experience, the river gorge at Marmol Cliff, springs and a viewpoint make it a fine choice for a simple nature trip.
Tuburan lies in northwestern Cebu Island, on the Tañon Strait side. Wikipedia puts it about
82 km

from Cebu City, and about 68,000 people live in its 54 barangays (2024 census). The large number of barangays reflects the many mountain villages; the smallest, Kanlunsing, has only a little over 200 residents. Wikipedia describes the municipality as having crystal-clear springs, beaches, creeks, rivers and caves here and there.

Tuburan is called the "Coffee Capital of Cebu." Coffee is grown on more than 3,000 hectares, and the Tuburan Coffee Farm in Barangay Kabangkalan, run by a farmers' cooperative, is known for an experience that shows the process from seed to cup. According to visitor accounts, if you contact the farm in advance you can be picked up and guided.

The history is interesting too. Don Mariano Montebon founded the town in 1851, and the town seat moved to its present site in 1857. It is the hometown of the revolutionary General Arcadio Maxilom, and in the Battle of Tuburan, which began on April 15, 1898, Spanish forces burned most of the town center. During World War II it was a guerrilla stronghold, and the Marmol Cliff caves and the Lantawan Tunnel are said to have served as shelters in that period. In 1953 Tabuelan split off as a separate municipality. Walking around the town church and park, you meet traces of this history everywhere, and asking local elders for old stories is part of the fun of traveling here.

Tuburan is not glamorous like Mactan or the city, but it is a simple place where coffee, nature and mountain scenery come together. It is less developed, so signs and facilities are limited, but that also means few people and a chance to feel local hospitality up close. Getting here from Cebu City is not easy, so we recommend allowing at least a day or more. The charm of Tuburan lies not in one or two individual attractions but in a slow trip over a day or two: smelling coffee beans at the farm in the morning, dipping your feet in a river in the afternoon, and having a warm meal at a town restaurant in the evening. It is a good place to rest away from the bustle of the city.

This coffee farm is run by a farmers' cooperative in Kabangkalan. It is known for an experience that introduces the process from planting seeds to picking and roasting the fruit. Contact them in advance to arrange your visit. The time when coffee cherries ripen red and the harvesting and processing seasons differ from year to year, so asking the farm is the most accurate way to plan your experience. You can also buy beans as souvenirs.

A huge limestone cliff standing along a river, named for its marble-like rock. Walking the shallow river between the cliffs is impressive, and there are said to be caves nearby. Go in the morning for good light and cooler temperatures. The riverbank and the foot of the cliff are slippery, so water shoes are better than sandals. If you are with children, keep an adult at their side.

A tunnel said to have served as an underground shelter from Japanese fighter-plane strafing during World War II. It is a historic site, but whether it is open to the public and whether it is safe have not been confirmed, so ask the municipal tourism office first. Tunnels and caves can have narrow, slippery entrances and require safety equipment and a guide.
A place to swim and snorkel in deep blue water. It is described as a deep pool known to locals, and visitors are advised to bring snorkeling gear. Because of the depth, wear a life jacket.

A cool spring welling up in the forest, good for swimming and picnics. Many travelers pack a lunch and eat by the water. The water is cold, which feels great on a hot day, but bring a towel so you do not get chilled.

From the summit you can see Tuburan town, nearby villages and the coastline in a 360-degree view. The hike is of moderate difficulty, and if you climb just before sunrise or just before sunset you can see the landscape in golden light. Before you climb, ask a local guide or your host about the route and timing. The path can be slippery just after rain.
A wide sandy shore with sunsets over the Tañon Strait. Bring snacks and a mat and you can spend relaxed time here. There are almost no facilities at the beach, so take your trash with you.

June 13 is the feast day of the parish patron, Saint Anthony of Padua, and the Tubod Festival is held. At cafes in town you can taste coffee grown in Tuburan. During the festival, lodging and transport get crowded, so plan early.
Leave the North Bus Terminal in Cebu City for Tuburan by V-Hire (van) or bus. The van via the Transcentral Highway is said to be the fastest.
Arrive in Tuburan town, leave your bags at your lodging and taste local coffee at a town cafe.
Have lunch at a local restaurant, then go to the Tuburan Coffee Farm for the experience.
Return to town, rest and have dinner.
Take a habal-habal to Marmol Cliff and walk the river gorge. Go only when the weather is good.
After lunch, swim at the Blue Hole or Mantawihan Spring.
Check the bus or van time back and set off.
The road to Marmol Cliff has unpaved sections, so it is safer to go in the dry season. If the weather is bad, drop the river and focus on the coffee farm and the town center.
Leave Cebu City by van.
Have breakfast in town and go to the coffee farm.
Do the coffee farm experience and tasting.
After lunch, look around Punta Beach or the town.
Take the van back to Cebu City.
From Manila (NAIA) to Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB), the direct flight takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
From the airport, go through Cebu City to the North Bus Terminal and take a ride to Tuburan.

items.title: Van or bus from Cebu City

children.text: The V-Hire via the Transcentral Highway (through Balamban) covers about
80 km
and is the fastest.
Ceres Liner goes via Lugo (Tabuelan) for about
100 km
, and Corominas Bros. goes via Toledo City for about
110 km
Check fares and times at the terminal.
The Transcentral Highway crosses the mountains, so it can take longer on foggy or rainy days.
Tuburan has many mountain roads, so a rental car or hired vehicle saves time.
For the gorge and springs outside town you need a habal-habal or a hired vehicle.
A hired vehicle is efficient for covering the gorge, springs and coffee farm in one day; negotiate the price with the driver.
Tricycles and habal-habal run in town. Negotiate the fare before you ride.
The dry season from December to May is best. Rivers and springs are clear and the unpaved roads are less muddy.
In the rainy season rivers swell and river gorges such as Marmol Cliff can be dangerous. Avoid the river when typhoons or heavy rain are forecast.

Timing your visit with the coffee harvest and processing seasons gives you more to see at the farm. The exact timing differs every year, so ask the farm. During the Tubod Festival week on June 13, the town is lively with parades and events.

and may vary with local conditions.
Lodging centers on small hotels and guesthouses in town. There are no big hotels, so book ahead in high season and festival time. Facilities are modest, so check air-conditioning and hot water.

The silog dishes at town restaurants are economical. Breakfast-friendly dishes such as tapsilog (beef, egg and rice) and tosilog (sweet cured pork, egg and rice) are easy to find at nearby restaurants. There are cafes in town serving Tuburan coffee, and buying local beans to take home is a good idea too.
There are few restaurants in the mountain areas, so bring a packed lunch and water before heading to springs or the gorge.

Lodging and restaurants are clustered along the town's main street, so you can walk between them. Going into mountain villages can make lodging difficult or limit meals, so plan your day around the town and hire a local guide to accompany you if needed. On weekends and holidays, more local family visitors can crowd the springs and beach.
Be sure to contact the coffee farm before you visit to confirm your schedule.
Marmol Cliff and the Blue Hole require water shoes and a change of clothes.
Near rivers, check the weather and water level, and do not enter if it rains.
Cash is necessary. Cards and ATMs are rare in mountain areas.
The viewpoint hike is best just before sunrise or just before sunset. Bring a flashlight.
During the June 13 festival, lodging gets crowded, so book ahead.
For historic sites such as the Lantawan Tunnel, ask the municipal tourism office whether they are open.
If you buy coffee beans in town, check the roasting date.
If you are prone to motion sickness on mountain roads, bring medicine beforehand.
Prepare cash, drinking water, snacks and medicine in town beforehand.
River gorges, springs and the Blue Hole can rise suddenly when it rains and are deep, so follow the advice of local guides.
The mountain roads wind and have unpaved sections.
Mobile signal is weak in some places, so download offline maps.
Road and facility conditions may have changed after the September 2025 Cebu earthquake.
Do not enter caves and tunnels without safety equipment.
Outside the town there are few signs and rescue facilities, so tell your lodging your plans and destination.
A big city about
82 km
to the east and the starting point for a Tuburan trip.
A neighboring municipality to the north that split off from Tuburan in 1953. The Ceres Liner route connects through this municipality on the road via Lugo.
A city on the route linking Cebu City and Tuburan by the Transcentral Highway. Vans cross this mountain pass to reach Tuburan.
A municipality along the coast to the northeast, which you pass when traveling between the west and the east.
